instruction: Include folders "/home/user/client" and "/home/user/server" in the workspace.

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding client-server architecture folders to workspace. Common pattern for full-stack applications with separate client and server codebases.
metadata.verification: Verified evaluator logic: check_json_settings checks workspace JSON for project, client, and server folders.

llm_judge_reasons: Expected value includes 'project' folder but instruction only asks to include 'client' and 'server' folders - evaluator checks for more than instruction requires
check_json_settings uses strict equality (!=) which will fail if workspace paths are absolute (/home/user/client) instead of relative (client), but VSCode accepts both formats
Strict array equality check will fail if folders are in different order than expected, even though order doesn't matter for workspace functionality
Evaluator will fail if there are additional folders beyond the three specified, which may be valid user state
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Remove 'project' folder from expected value since instruction doesn't require it, OR update instruction to explicitly mention all three folders
Use a more flexible comparison that checks if required folders are present (subset check) rather than exact equality
Handle both absolute and relative path formats in the comparison logic
Consider checking folder presence rather than exact array equality to handle order variations
